events.title: Giordano Bruno Burned at the Stake
events.description: Italian philosopher, mathematician, and former Dominican friar Giordano Bruno was burned at the stake in the Campo de' Fiori in Rome after the Roman Inquisition convicted him of heresy. His views included the infinity of the universe and a plurality of worlds.
events.significance: Bruno became a symbol of the conflict between free thought and religious orthodoxy, and is often remembered as a martyr for science and intellectual freedom.

events.title: H.L. Hunley Sinks the USS Housatonic
events.description: During the American Civil War, the Confederate submarine H.L. Hunley attacked and sank the Union warship USS Housatonic off Charleston, South Carolina, using a spar torpedo. The Hunley also sank soon afterward with all hands lost.
events.significance: It was the first time in history that a submarine sank an enemy warship, foreshadowing the importance of submarine warfare in later conflicts.

events.title: First Ship Passes Through the Suez Canal Area Opening Preparations
events.description: On February 17, 1867, the first ship, a steamer, transited the partially completed Suez Canal route during construction, a milestone ahead of the canal's formal opening in 1869.
events.significance: The milestone showed that a sea-level canal linking the Mediterranean and Red Seas was feasible, reshaping global trade routes.

events.title: Nixon Departs for Historic Visit to China
events.description: U.S. President Richard Nixon left Washington on February 17, 1972, for a landmark trip to the People's Republic of China, arriving in Beijing on February 21 and meeting Chairman Mao Zedong.
events.significance: The visit ended more than two decades of diplomatic isolation between the United States and China and fundamentally shifted Cold War geopolitics.

events.title: Kosovo Declares Independence from Serbia
events.description: The Assembly of Kosovo declared independence from Serbia on February 17, 2008, establishing Kosovo as a sovereign state.
events.significance: The declaration was recognized by many countries but opposed by Serbia, Russia, and others, and it remains a major point of international legal and political dispute.
